fichas.title: Lifts: principles and drive systems
fichas.summary: Position lifts at the source of traffic flow, allow sufficient space for waiting and queuing without obstructing stairs, and connect them carefully to traffic routes. The page illustrates traction and hydraulic drive arrangements. Traction lifts ideally have the drive above the shaft; hydraulic lifts commonly use a push cylinder, while pull-cylinder arrangements are also shown.

fichas.title: Lift door-opening types and shaft width
fichas.summary: The diagrams relate sliding-door configurations to shaft width. A one-sided telescopic sliding door is described with a shaft-width formula and a minimum value; a centrally opening sliding door has a separate formula and minimum. Four-part telescopic doors depend on the drive type, while six-part telescopic doors are suited to cars with wide openings, including in hospitals and commercial buildings.

fichas.title: Lift plans and shaft dimensions
fichas.summary: Plans show standard, wheelchair-suitable, through-loading, double, and triple lift arrangements. The diagrams print car, shaft, and depth dimensions; the standard plan also indicates a 630 kg, 8-person car. The double and triple arrangements show repeated shaft-width dimensions and separation notation.
